questions.q: Evaluate $\int 2x(x^2+1)^4\,dx$ using the substitution $u=x^2+1$.
Evaluate $\int_0^{\pi/2}\sin^3x\cos x\,dx$ using the substitution $u=\sin x$.
Evaluate $\int x e^x\,dx$ using integration by parts.
questions.answer: Let $u=x$, $dv=e^x\,dx$, so $du=dx$, $v=e^x$. $\int xe^x\,dx=xe^x-\int e^x\,dx=xe^x-e^x+C=(x-1)e^x+C$.

questions.q: Evaluate $\int x\ln x\,dx$ using integration by parts.
questions.answer: Let $u=\ln x$, $dv=x\,dx$, so $du=(1/x)\,dx$, $v=x^2/2$. $\int x\ln x\,dx=x^2/2\ln x-\int x^2/2\cdot1/x\,dx=x^2/2\ln x-x^2/4+C$.

questions.q: Evaluate $\int x^2e^x\,dx$, applying integration by parts twice.
questions.answer: First application: $u=x^2$, $dv=e^xdx$: $\int x^2e^x\,dx=x^2e^x-\int2xe^x\,dx$. From the previous problem, $\int xe^x\,dx=(x-1)e^x+C$, so $\int2xe^x\,dx=2(x-1)e^x$. Result: $x^2e^x-2(x-1)e^x+C=(x^2-2x+2)e^x+C$.

questions.q: Evaluate $\int\cos^2x\,dx$ using the identity $\cos^2x=(1+\cos2x)/2$.
Evaluate $\int1/(x^2-1)\,dx$ by first expressing the integrand in partial fractions.
Evaluate $\int_1^e\ln x/x\,dx$, using the substitution $u=\ln x$.
Evaluate $\int_0^{\pi}x\sin x\,dx$ using integration by parts.
questions.answer: Let $u=x$, $dv=\sin x\,dx$, so $du=dx$, $v=-\cos x$. $\int x\sin x\,dx=-x\cos x+\int\cos x\,dx=-x\cos x+\sin x$. Evaluating from $0$ to $\pi$: $[-\pi\cos\pi+\sin\pi]-[0+0]=-\pi(-1)+0=\pi$.

questions.q: Evaluate $\int1/(1+x^2)\,dx$, and use it to evaluate $\int_0^1 1/(1+x^2)\,dx$.
questions.answer: $\int1/(1+x^2)\,dx=\arctan x+C$. So $\int_0^1 1/(1+x^2)\,dx=\arctan(1)-\arctan(0)=\pi/4-0=\pi/4$.

sections.heading: Integration by substitution with trigonometric functions

questions.q: Evaluate $\int\sin^3x\,dx$, using the identity $\sin^2x=1-\cos^2x$ and the substitution $u=\cos x$.
questions.answer: Rewrite: $\sin^3x=\sin x(1-\cos^2x)$. Let $u=\cos x$, $du=-\sin x\,dx$. $\int\sin x(1-\cos^2x)\,dx=-\int(1-u^2)\,du=-u+u^3/3+C=-\cos x+\cos^3x/3+C$.

questions.q: Evaluate $\int\tan x\,dx$, using the substitution $u=\cos x$.
questions.answer: $\tan x=\sin x/(\cos x)$. Let $u=\cos x$, $du=-\sin x\,dx$. $\int\sin x/(\cos x)\,dx=-\int1/u\,du=-\ln|u|+C=-\ln|\cos x|+C=\ln|\sec x|+C$.

sections.heading: Integration by parts with a logarithmic integrand

questions.q: Evaluate $\int_1^e\ln x\,dx$ using integration by parts.
questions.answer: Let $u=\ln x$, $dv=dx$, so $du=(1/x)\,dx$, $v=x$. $\int\ln x\,dx=x\ln x-\int x\cdot1/x\,dx=x\ln x-x+C$. Evaluating from $1$ to $e$: $[e\ln e-e]-[1\ln1-1]=(e-e)-(0-1)=0+1=1$.

questions.q: Evaluate $\int1/(5+4\cos x)\,dx$ using the substitution $t=\tan(x/2)$, given that this substitution transforms $\cos x=(1-t^2)/(1+t^2)$ and $dx=2/(1+t^2)dt$, leading to the simplified integrand $2/(9+t^2)$.
questions.answer: Substituting: $\int1/(5+4(1-t^2)/(1+t^2))\cdot2/(1+t^2)\,dt=\int2/(5(1+t^2)+4(1-t^2))\,dt=\int2/(9+t^2)\,dt$. Using the standard result $\int1/(a^2+t^2)\,dt=(1/a)\arctan(t/a)+C$ with $a=3$: $2\cdot(1/3)\arctan(t/3)+C=(2/3)\arctan((1/3)\tan(x/2))+C$.

sections.heading: Integration by parts with a trigonometric-exponential product

questions.q: Evaluate $\int e^x\cos x\,dx$, applying integration by parts twice and solving the resulting equation for the original integral.
questions.answer: Let $I=\int e^x\cos x\,dx$. First application: $u=\cos x$, $dv=e^xdx$, so $du=-\sin x\,dx$, $v=e^x$: $I=e^x\cos x+\int e^x\sin x\,dx$. Second application on $\int e^x\sin x\,dx$: $u=\sin x$, $dv=e^xdx$: $\int e^x\sin x\,dx=e^x\sin x-\int e^x\cos x\,dx=e^x\sin x-I$. Substituting back: $I=e^x\cos x+e^x\sin x-I$, so $2I=e^x(\cos x+\sin x)$, giving $I=e^x(\cos x+\sin x)/2+C$.

sections.heading: Finding the area between two curves using integration

questions.q: Find the area of the region enclosed between $y=\sin x$ and $y=\cos x$ for $\pi/4\leq x\leq5\pi/4$ (the interval on which $\sin x\geq\cos x$).
questions.answer: Area $=\int_{\pi/4}^{5\pi/4}(\sin x-\cos x)\,dx=[-\cos x-\sin x]_{\pi/4}^{5\pi/4}$. At $x=5\pi/4$: $-\cos5\pi/4-\sin5\pi/4=\sqrt{2}/2+\sqrt{2}/2=\sqrt{2}$. At $x=\pi/4$: $-\cos\pi/4-\sin\pi/4=-\sqrt{2}/2-\sqrt{2}/2=-\sqrt{2}$. Area $=\sqrt{2}-(-\sqrt{2})=2\sqrt{2}$.

questions.q: Evaluate $\int x^2\ln x\,dx$ using integration by parts.
questions.answer: Let $u=\ln x$, $dv=x^2dx$, so $du=(1/x)\,dx$, $v=x^3/3$. $\int x^2\ln x\,dx=x^3/3\ln x-\int x^3/3\cdot1/x\,dx=x^3/3\ln x-\int x^2/3\,dx=x^3/3\ln x-x^3/9+C$.

questions.q: A particle's velocity is given by $v(t)=t\cos t$ metres per second. Find the particle's displacement over the interval $0\leq t\leq\pi$, using integration by parts.
questions.answer: Displacement $=\int_0^{\pi}t\cos t\,dt$. Using integration by parts with $u=t$, $dv=\cos t\,dt$, so $du=dt$, $v=\sin t$: $\int t\cos t\,dt=t\sin t-\int\sin t\,dt=t\sin t+\cos t+C$. Evaluating from $0$ to $\pi$: $[\pi\sin\pi+\cos\pi]-[0\sin0+\cos0]=[0-1]-[0+1]=-1-1=-2$. Displacement $=-2$ metres.

questions.q: This question has three parts. (a) Use the substitution $u=x^2+4$ to find $\int x/(x^2+4)\,dx$. (b) Use integration by parts to find $\int\arctan x\,dx$. (c) Hence, using the result of part (b) and the standard result $\int1/(1+x^2)dx=\arctan x+C$, evaluate $\int_0^1\arctan x\,dx$, giving an exact answer in terms of $\pi$ and $\ln$.
questions.answer: (a) $u=x^2+4$, $du=2x\,dx$: $\int x/(x^2+4)\,dx=1/2\int1/u\,du=1/2\ln|x^2+4|+C$. (b) Let $u=\arctan x$, $dv=dx$, so $du=(1/(1+x^2))\,dx$, $v=x$: $\int\arctan x\,dx=x\arctan x-\int x/(1+x^2)\,dx=x\arctan x-1/2\ln(1+x^2)+C$ (using the result from part (a), with $4$ replaced by $1$). (c) Evaluating from $0$ to $1$: $[1\cdot\arctan1-1/2\ln2]-[0-1/2\ln1]=\pi/4-1/2\ln2$.

questions.q: Given the reduction formula $I_n=\int x^ne^x\,dx=x^ne^x-nI_{n-1}$ (obtained via integration by parts), and that $I_0=e^x+C$, use it to find $I_2=\int x^2e^x\,dx$.
questions.answer: $I_1=x^1e^x-1\cdot I_0=xe^x-e^x$ (ignoring the constant until the final step). $I_2=x^2e^x-2I_1=x^2e^x-2(xe^x-e^x)=x^2e^x-2xe^x+2e^x+C=(x^2-2x+2)e^x+C$, matching the result found earlier in this worksheet by direct repeated integration by parts.

sections.heading: Integration using the sine double-angle identity

questions.q: Evaluate $\int\sin^2x\,dx$ using the identity $\sin^2x=(1-\cos2x)/2$.
The region bounded by $y=\sqrt{x}$, the $x$-axis, and $x=4$ is rotated $360^\circ$ about the $x$-axis. Find the volume of the resulting solid, using $V=\pi\int_0^4y^2\,dx$.
questions.answer: Since $y=\sqrt{x}$, $y^2=x$. $V=\pi\int_0^4x\,dx=\pi[x^2/2]_0^4=\pi(8-0)=8\pi$ cubic units.

sections.heading: Substitution with a shifting definite integral bound

questions.q: Evaluate $\int_0^1x\sqrt{x^2+1}\,dx$ using the substitution $u=x^2+1$.
questions.answer: $du=2x\,dx$, so $x\,dx=du/2$. When $x=0$, $u=1$; when $x=1$, $u=2$. So the integral becomes $\int\sqrt{u}\cdot(1/2)\,du$, with $u$ running from $1$ to $2$. Since $\int\sqrt{u}\,du=(2/3)u^{3/2}+C$, this gives $(1/2)(2/3)(2^{3/2}-1)=(1/3)(2\sqrt{2}-1)$.

questions.q: Which integration technique is most appropriate for evaluating $\int x^3\sin x\,dx$?
choices: Integration by parts, applied three times (reducing the power of $x$ each time)
questions.answer: Since the integrand is a product of a polynomial and a trigonometric function, integration by parts is appropriate — and because the polynomial factor is $x^3$ (not $x^1$), the process must be repeated three times, each time reducing the power of $x$ by one, until the polynomial factor disappears.
